findings.finding: Quadient contractually committed, in its own communique, to give a status update on the strategic review of its Lockers business ON THIS RELEASE (23 September 2026) -- with Rothschild & Co, Societe Generale and Darrois Villey already mandated at launch -- and only part of the deal option is still in the price: the stock rose +6.00% on the 20 July announcement and peaked at EUR 13.68 on 3 August (+14.0% vs EUR 12.00 pre-announcement) but sits at EUR 12.46 today, so roughly two thirds of the peak premium has bled out ahead of the one date the company itself named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is exactly one prior instance of this line and it is the launch itself: 2026-07-20, the stock closed +6.00% at EUR 12.72 on 96,222 shares against a 60-day median of 37,606 (2.6x), then drifted to EUR 13.68 by 3 August. The line has never been tested by an UPDATE, which is why my band is wide in both directions: the modal outcome is 'process continues, no decision', a signed or near-signed disposal is the fat right tail, and 'we will retain and invest' is the left tail. The path to the equity is stated rather than assumed: net debt was EUR 682m at 31 January 2026 at 3.0x leverage including leasing (1.6x excluding), against a EUR 429m market capitalisation on 34,468,912 shares, so a disposal near the EUR 180m French estimate cuts net debt by about a quarter and removes the balance-sheet overhang that French coverage names as the single biggest concern on the name.

findings.finding: Quadient voluntarily pre-disclosed a strongly positive operational datapoint about the quarter being reported -- Digital global bookings up more than 20% year on year like-for-like in Q2, with French e-invoicing bookings up more than ten-fold -- four weeks before the print and before the quiet period opened, which materially lowers the probability of the FY2026 guidance cut that is this stock's only demonstrated -15% trigger.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is the whole reaction function on this name and it is cleanly measured over three events. FY2025 guidance CUT at the H1 2025 print (filed 2025-09-24 after the close; 'FY 2025 revenue is now expected to decline by a low single digit on an organic basis', replacing 'acceleration in organic revenue growth') -> EUR 15.94 to EUR 13.10, -17.82%. FY2025 results with a EUR 124m Mail goodwill impairment (filed 2026-03-25 after the close) -> EUR 12.68 to EUR 10.88, -14.20%. FY2026 guidance CONFIRMED at Q1 (filed 2026-05-21 after the close) -> EUR 11.98 to EUR 12.34, +3.01%. So this stock pays roughly +3% for a confirmation and roughly -15% for a cut: sharply asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the reason my emitted move is far below the upside of my band.

findings.finding: The AMF published a 'franchissement de seuils' on Quadient on 21 September 2026 -- two days before the print, in French only, with no English wire version -- whose headline (a holder crossing DOWN through 5%) reads far more negative than the arithmetic inside it: Janus Henderson Investors UK sold only 32,062 shares, 1.8% of its holding, and still holds 1,709,808 shares or 4.96%, having crossed UP through 5% on 23 July by buying on market three sessions after the Lockers review was announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable on this name: the AMF short register has never named Quadient (anchor_covered false, register_read_no_position), so there is no disclosed-short history to read a squeeze or a cover off, and threshold declarations on a EUR 429m small cap do not normally carry a same-week price signature. findings.finding: The asset being put up for review is trading badly on the line a buyer pays for: Quadient's own Q1 2026 release discloses that Lockers non-recurring revenue fell 44.6% organically, taking the whole Lockers segment to -3.8% organic after +11.2% in H1 2025, and French coverage explicitly names this as the concern hanging over the 23 September checkpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The market has already been shown this exact number once and looked straight through it: the -44.6% was disclosed in the 21 May 2026 Q1 release and the stock rose +3.01% the next session, because subscription revenue in the same segment grew 18% organically and is now 80% of Lockers revenue against two thirds in FY2025. That is the single strongest argument for sizing this small, and it is why I cut it rather than carrying it at a full point. Its live bite is narrower: the FY2026 guide contains an explicit 'EBITDA margin above 10% in Lockers' target, up from 5.0% in FY2025, and a second weak hardware quarter puts that specific line at risk on a name that pays roughly -15% for a guidance cut.

The two prints that followed weakness (2025-04-29, -3.70%) were milder. Small n, and stated as such.

findings.finding: Barry M was bought on 9 February 2026 for GBP1.4m cash, including 'its IP, stock and order book, but excluding the manufacturing capabilities and any liabilities' -- a brand with GBP15-17.4m of annual turnover and one-metre-plus stands in 1,300 UK stores. No fair value allocation has ever been published: the FY25 annual report carries it only as a bare post-balance-sheet note. If the identifiable net assets acquired (inventory plus the order book plus brand IP) fair-value above GBP1.4m, IFRS 3 forces a gain on bargain purchase straight through the H1 income statement, which would flatter statutory PBT against a weak underlying half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Barry M headline itself is the only positive print in the observed five: 2026-02-09 'Acquisition of Barry M brand & FY25 Trading Update' +10.50%, on a day that also carried a weak trading statement. So this market has paid for Barry M news before. No prior exceptional-credit instance to score.

findings.finding: The TR-1 record shows the largest non-insider holder adding into the print and a smaller one trimming: Schroders plc went 10.040844% -> 11.086664% on 16 June 2026, the day of the AGM statement; Rathbones Investment Management went 5.575700% -> 4.996700% on 6 July 2026. Against a concert party (Bazini, Macleod, Rodol and relatives) of about 39.73%, that leaves a genuinely thin free float -- roughly 44% once Schroders and Rathbones are removed -- which is the mechanical reason this name prints double-digit reactions on USD 384k of daily turnover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior instance. Recorded here because it is the only disclosed positioning that exists for this name -- the FCA short register does not name it -- and because it is the main reason I did not size the negative findings closer to the 10.5% median.

outside_window.finding: The GBP2.5m buyback is 89-98% spent and its bid disappears within about two weeks. Treasury reached 1,116,967 shares by 16 September; the 3 August tranche went at a 187.59p VWAP and everything after it traded in a 200-223p band, which bounds cumulative consideration at GBP2.22m-GBP2.46m of the GBP2.5m maximum. At the recent pace (86,371 shares in the week to 11 September, 50,685 in three days to 16 September) the authority is exhausted in early October, removing a buyer that has been ~19% of daily volume. Real and sourceable, and worth nothing to a one-session window.

The entire FY26 second-half case rests on events that settle after this print: the Dirk Rossmann pilot across 2,200 German stores (launched May 2026, reorder decision H2), the 'significantly improved' Walmart Christmas order, the Ulta Beauty online Christmas gift range, and Barry M's first re-sourced production run after the London factory was excluded from the acquisition. Christmas sell-through is a December/January fact.

lessons_applied: 'Two findings resting on one document are one finding' -- merged the four-month sales decline and the GBP5.7m non-repeating 2025 comparative into a single net -3.0 finding, since both come out of the FY25 annual report. Findings count 6 -> 5, sum unchanged at -6.2.

'Keep findings inside the exit window' -- split the buyback: the price level going in stays in findings (-1.2, resolves 2026-09-23), the programme's exhaustion in early October moved to outside_window at -2.0 where it earns nothing.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number' -- expected_move moved from -5.5 to -5.0, visibly smaller than the -6.2 sum, with the 1.2-point haircut and its three reasons written into conviction_note rather than left implicit.

'A truncated zero is not a measurement' -- rewrote positioning_check to say the register was read and does not name this issuer, and to state that there is no building/covering signal at all, instead of reporting 0.0% short as a fact about Warpaint.

'A one_off with no stated path to the guide is sized at a fraction' -- held the Barry M bargain-purchase finding at +0.5 against an underlying half worth multiples of it, and said in the finding why (adjusted EBITDA excludes it).

'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error' and 'coverage tells you which regime you are in' -- checked the emitted -5.0 against this name's own distribution (median |move| 10.5%, max 19.17%, 4 of 5 negative) and against a 3-analyst band in which 2 of 3 are house brokers, and did NOT cut it further despite genuine two-sidedness.
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series' -- dropped a UK beauty-market/consumer-demand angle entirely rather than size macro-to-company transmission the company has not asserted.
